title: Florida House, District 27
what_it_does: Represents District 27 in the Florida House of Representatives; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: Provisional: Florida Politics reported on June 8, 2026 (four days before candidate qualifying closed at noon June 12) that the incumbent had drawn no opponent. Whether anyone qualified in the final days could NOT be verified in this sandbox (Division of Elections, Ballotpedia and Wikipedia were blocked), so treat 'not on ballot' as provisional.
verified_ballot_note: Florida Politics (June 8, 2026) listed HD 27 (R+37; parts of Lake, Marion and Volusia counties) among seats where incumbent Republican Rep. Richard Gentry faced no opposition ahead of the June 12 qualifying deadline (https://floridapolitics.com/archives/800374-with-qualifying-days-away-5-competitive-house-seats-remain-unchallenged/). Final qualifying status not verified. Research limitation: every WebFetch (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, Division of Elections, county SOEs, news sites) was blocked and the search budget was capped, so this roster comes only from search-result snippets and should be re-verified against the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Richard Gentry
candidates.background: Incumbent Republican state representative for HD 27, which spans parts of Lake, Marion and Volusia counties. Reported unopposed as of June 8, 2026.

taxes.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

property_tax.summary: Voted for CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; a vote to refer the amendment is coded as leaning.

immigration.summary: Voted for SB 2-C (2025), the February 2025 special-session immigration law that created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, made entering Florida as an unauthorized immigrant a state crime and required local cooperation with federal detention.
